title: Evaluation of a layered Boolean gate
statement: Let $g$ be a Boolean DAG gate whose argument list has no repetitions, with exactly one argument if it is a NOT gate, and suppose $g$ is not an OR gate. Let $D$ be a type, let $e$ assign an element of $D$ to each argument position in the list, let $v:D\to\mathrm{Fin}\,2$, and let $w$ be a Boolean list. If, for every argument index $a$ of $g$, the value $v(e(a))$ is the $0$–$1$ encoding of the value of $w$ at index $a$ (taking that value to be false when the index is out of range), then the gate on $D$ constructed from $g$ and $e$, evaluated using $v$, equals the $0$–$1$ encoding of the evaluation of $g$ on $w$.
hypotheses_covered: The argument list of $g$ has no repetitions
If $g$ is a NOT gate, its argument list has length one
The embedding assigns an element of $D$ to each argument occurrence
For every listed argument, its assigned value is the encoding of the list value at that index, with false for out-of-range indices
